_by_key: A big round face changes mood - happy, calm, sad, wow - each change wipes a new background colour across the frame while the eyes and mouth morph, the face squashes and the mood's name drops in; a marker slides along a scale.
A block of one line repeated; its letters burst apart across the frame, drift loose, and fly back into the block one after another.
A button pops in, a cursor glides to it on a curve, presses (a dip and a ripple) and the button changes - Subscribe turns grey Subscribed and a bell pops and rings.

A camera viewfinder over your video: corner brackets, a blinking red REC dot, a timecode that runs frame by frame, camera info and a battery, a focus box that snaps onto the middle. Loops at any length.
A caption per story (| between; empty = none)
A card - a dark note, a terminal window or paper - swings in tilted; its text types in letter by letter behind a cursor, the card floats and slowly straightens.
A chat that builds message by message: each bubble grows out of its corner, its words fade in a moment later, the replies come after typing dots - green on beige, blue on white or dark.
A check badge after the name
A check mark that draws itself

A countdown item for a top-5 / top-10 video: 'TOP 5 EDITING TRICKS' on top, a huge outlined number slams in and fills with colour from the bottom, the item's title wipes in under it, a light streak crosses the number; it pushes out at the end.
A countdown: each number pops in and the ring around it drains over its step, a glow pulses on every change, the end word lands with a kick - or a number beside a line that shrinks.
A dark app card swings in in 3D, its total counts up, a change badge pops, bars grow with a highlight walking across them (or a line with a soft area); the card floats with a slow tilt.
A departures board: every tile flips through letters until it lands on its own, left to right and row after row, so the words settle like a wave.

A desktop folder pops in, a cursor glides to it and double-clicks, and a window grows out of it with a grid of pictures popping in - a portfolio, a project, behind the scenes; it can close back at the end.

A finished title screen in four looks: an editorial title with a big serif word whose letters rise and breathe; an event card with words rising over a soft shape; two names with an ampersand blurring in (an invitation); or a product line with a sound-wave strip and a button popping.
A focus box snaps in the middle

A hand-drawn mark over your video - a circle round something, an underline, an arrow, a check, a cross or a scribble - drawn stroke by stroke by a pencil whose tip rides the line, with an optional handwritten note; then the pencil lifts away.
A handwritten note beside it (empty = none)
A heart pops (it overshoots and settles), a ring goes out, small particles burst and fade, a +1 floats up and the count ticks up; then it beats gently.
A label in the middle (empty = none)
A line drawn over the bars
A line that draws itself: a chart whose lines rise with a dot riding each tip and the end value popping; a wavy journey with milestones popping and a flag; or a heartbeat line drawing across.
A line under the face (empty = none)
A line under the pile (empty = none)
A line with a soft area
A list on a wheel: items roll up past the middle one at a time; the current one bold and dark, the rest smaller and fainter with distance, like a phone's picker.
A list that builds one line at a time: a check draws itself (or a box is ticked, a number, a dot), the words slide in beside it, the list re-centres as it grows; earlier lines can fade back.
A logo sting: a rounded square drops, lands with a squash, turns into a circle and the letter (or your logo) appears in it, the name fades up under it - or the mark spins in.

A loose pile of cards shuffles - the top card slides out and goes under, again and again - then one card comes forward, straightens and lights up with a glowing edge while the rest dim. Payments, membership, picks, a reveal.
A map pin drops and bounces, rings pulse out from its point the whole time, a place card pops up above it; optionally a map whose streets draw themselves in first.
A map under it (streets drawn in)
A month card pops in and its days fill one after another with coloured dots, a streak counter ticking with them - a habit, a posting plan, a countdown to a date.

A news-style band: a BREAKING tag snaps in, the headline bar wipes out of it, a ticker scrolls its lines underneath, a live dot blinks; it leaves the way it came. For a funny breaking-news beat or a real update.
A one- or two-line title whose letters never stand still: a wave of squash and stretch runs through them, or they boil like a hand drawing; the second line in four colours.
A phone rises and floats while a list fills its screen row by row - each row slides in from the right and its icon pops; at the end the rows can slide away. Apps, features, steps, tips.
A photobooth strip pushes down in jerks, frame by frame, in black and white or colour, sways on the wall with a handwritten date, then slides back up - memories, a recap, friends.

A phrase types in, but some letters are small coloured shapes - a triangle, a circle, a square - that spin in where the letter would be, bob while it holds, and turn back into their letters at the end.

A post-style quote card - a round picture, a name with a check badge, a handle - pops in with a tilt that settles; the quote comes in word by word, the starred phrase in the accent colour; the counts tick up.

A review: a card rises, the stars pop in one after another and fill (a half star fills half), the quote appears word by word, the reviewer's picture and name slide in, a score line comes in under the card.
A ring of dots that turns, breaks into a cloud of stars drifting across the frame, then pulls back into the ring with a glow as it closes - a loading moment, a 'thinking' beat, a transition.
A rubber wobble in the middle
A sale: a card pops up, the old price gets struck through, the new price slams in, a spiky -50 % burst spins onto the corner and keeps turning, confetti falls once, a button pops and pulses.
A sci-fi status line: each letter scrambles through random signs before it locks, glitches jolt it now and then with a colour split, small lines type in, scan lines roll.
A sign flickers off and on during the hold
A small cross in the middle

A social poll: the card pops, the question and the answers come in, a tap picks one with a ripple, then every answer's bar fills to its share with the percent counting - the tapped one ticked, the winner in the accent colour.

A social profile card rises: the picture pops inside a turning story ring, the name and handle slide in, the posts / followers / following count up, the bio appears, and the Follow button gets clicked and turns to Following.
A soft disc behind the heart
A soft gradient blob that never stops changing shape - it breathes, turns and drifts, its colours rotate, a few sparks float - a background for words, a logo or a talking head.

A song card: a vinyl disc with the cover spins, the title (scrolling when long) and artist under it, a progress bar and the time counting, play controls - everything pulsing on the beat; or a visualizer whose bars jump on every beat.
A speech bubble pops out of its tail and pulses (a dip and a colour flip every 24 frames), or a round pill with an emoji that waves - a message, a reaction, a callout next to someone talking.
A story or a quote told card by card: lines fade up out of a blur one after another, the key words bright; or a colour per card with one big serif keyword typed, slid or risen in.
A string of lights at the top
A string through them once they line up
A switch pops in off and flips on - the knob slides with a squash, the track turns green and glows, the word under it changes; it can flip on, off and on again.
A tall word slams in, then its letters come loose one after another - each wobbles, tips over and falls out of the frame spinning; the letters that stay are left alone.
A title pops when a chapter starts
A title that changes into another: the first one's letters leave along a wave one after another while the second's ride the same wave in and settle.
A transition made of square pixels: blobs grow from a few spots until the frame is one colour, then shrink away blob by blob to reveal the words (or the next shot) - stepped like a pixel animation.

A transition to put over a cut: bars, a circle, a slanted panel, two halves or thin stripes cover the frame in two colours, hold, then clear the other way - the cut goes where it is fully covered. Words can show while it covers.

A trip: the start pin drops with its name, a dashed route draws in a curve to the destination with a plane (or a glowing dot) riding its tip and turning with it, the end pin pops with a ripple. A drawn map, or none over your own.

A video's chapters as a segmented progress bar along the bottom (or top): it fills as the video plays, the current chapter stands taller and a small '02 · Setup' title pops when each chapter starts. Give it the video's length.
A white border, like a print
A year or a number as the whole frame: rising in glowing over a liquid wave rolling at the bottom; or two huge lines that shrink in hard steps to a small mono line.
Accent (a dot on the i, the first letter...)
Accent (pastel and light: the key words)
Accent (the number, the glow, the chart)

An editorial page: a kicker, a serif headline whose key words get a highlighter sweep word after word, the text rising in under it and a row of three numbers.
An envelope slides in, its wax seal pops off, the flap opens and a letter rises out and comes to the front with its handwritten lines appearing - an invitation, a thank-you, an announcement.

Bars grow from the base one after another with a slow end, each value counting up on its bar; up / down bars in green and red; an optional line drawn across the tops.

One big word turns to grain - its edge breaks up, the grains scatter and thin out - then gathers back; or forms out of dust; or blows away sideways; small words frame it at the corners.
One bold word stacked; the middle copy comes in stretched and skewed like rubber, snaps into a clean stack, wobbles once and stretches away.

One icon pops in and keeps pulsing: an app-style tile with letters (like an editing app's icon), a red warning sign that shakes, or a round symbol - a ring goes out and the glow breathes on every pulse.

Phone stories: pictures (yours, or soft colour fills) play one after another full screen with the progress bars filling at the top, the name in the corner, a quick zoom on each cut and a slow push-in, a tilted caption sticker popping on each.
Phones drop onto a pile one after another, then fan out like cards with the middle one forward, each showing a picture (yours or a colour) - an app showcase, several screens, a content mix.

Point at things in your video: a dot lands on a spot and pulses, a line draws out from it with an elbow, and a title with a small line slides out of its end - several one after another; they draw back at the end.

Progress you can see: a ring fills to its percent with the number counting and a check popping; a ring drawing around a symbol that pops and glows; or a ticket card whose bar fills with a glowing tip.

Real logos of the logo library: your stack, the platforms you post on, the tools a video is about or the clients you worked with - a grid of app tiles popping in one after another, an endless sliding strip, or one big logo at a time, each replacing the last, with the names under them.

A big round face changes mood - happy, c: Una cara grande y redonda cambia de ánimo - feliz, tranquila, triste, alucinada - cada cambio barre el fotograma con un color de fondo nuevo mientras los ojos y la boca se transforman, la cara se aplasta y cae el nombre del estado de ánimo; un marcador se desliza por una escala.
A block of one line repeated; its letter: Un bloque de una línea repetida; sus letras estallan por el fotograma, flotan sueltas y vuelven volando al bloque una tras otra.
A button pops in, a cursor glides to it: Aparece un botón, un cursor se desliza hasta él en curva y lo pulsa (se hunde y sale una onda), y el botón cambia - Suscribirse pasa a un Suscrito gris y aparece una campana que suena.
A camera viewfinder over your video: cor: Un visor de cámara sobre tu vídeo: esquinas marcadas, un punto rojo de REC que parpadea, un código de tiempo que avanza fotograma a fotograma, los datos de la cámara y una batería, un recuadro de enfoque que se ajusta al centro. Hace bucle con cualquier duración.
A caption per story (| between; empty =: Un texto por historia (separa con |; vacío = nada)
A card - a dark note, a terminal window: Una tarjeta - una nota oscura, una ventana de terminal o un papel - entra girando, inclinada; su texto se teclea letra a letra tras un cursor, la tarjeta flota y se endereza despacio.
A chat that builds message by message: e: Un chat que se forma mensaje a mensaje: cada burbuja crece desde su esquina, sus palabras aparecen un momento después y las respuestas llegan tras los puntos de «escribiendo» - verde sobre beis, azul sobre blanco u oscuro.
A check badge after the name: Una insignia de verificado tras el nombre
A check mark that draws itself: Un check que se dibuja solo
A countdown item for a top-5 / top-10 vi: Un puesto de la cuenta atrás de un vídeo de top 5 / top 10: 'TOP 5 TRUCOS DE EDICIÓN' arriba, un número enorme con contorno entra de golpe y se llena de color desde abajo, el título del puesto aparece debajo y un destello cruza el número; al final sale empujado.
A countdown: each number pops in and the: Una cuenta atrás: cada número aparece y el anillo que lo rodea se vacía durante su paso, un brillo late en cada cambio y la palabra final aterriza con un golpe - o un número junto a una línea que se encoge.
A cursor clicks them: Un cursor hace clic en ellos
A dark app card swings in in 3D, its tot: Una tarjeta oscura de app entra girando en 3D, su total sube contando, aparece una etiqueta de cambio y crecen unas barras con un brillo que las recorre (o una línea con un área suave); la tarjeta flota con una inclinación lenta.
A departures board: every tile flips thr: Un panel de salidas: cada ficha va pasando letras hasta que se para en la suya, de izquierda a derecha y fila tras fila, así que las palabras se asientan como una ola.
A desktop folder pops in, a cursor glide: Aparece una carpeta de escritorio, un cursor se desliza hasta ella y hace doble clic, y de ella crece una ventana en la que aparece una cuadrícula de imágenes - un portfolio, un proyecto, el detrás de las cámaras; al final puede volver a cerrarse.
A finished title screen in four looks: a: Una cartela de título acabada en cuatro looks: un título editorial con una gran palabra serif cuyas letras suben y respiran; una tarjeta de evento con palabras que suben sobre una forma suave; dos nombres con un & que aparece desde un desenfoque (una invitación); o una línea de producto con una tira de onda de sonido y un botón que aparece.
A focus box snaps in the middle: Un recuadro de enfoque se ajusta en el centro
A hand-drawn mark over your video - a ci: Una marca dibujada a mano sobre tu vídeo - un círculo alrededor de algo, un subrayado, una flecha, un check, una cruz o un garabato - trazo a trazo, con un lápiz cuya punta sigue la línea y una nota manuscrita si quieres; luego el lápiz se levanta y se va.
A handwritten note beside it (empty = no: Una nota manuscrita al lado (vacío = nada)
A heart pops (it overshoots and settles): Aparece un corazón (se pasa de tamaño y se asienta), sale un anillo, unas partículas pequeñas estallan y se desvanecen, sube flotando un +1 y el contador avanza; después late suavemente.
A label in the middle (empty = none): Una etiqueta en el centro (vacío = nada)
A Like button first: Primero un botón de Me gusta
A line drawn over the bars: Una línea dibujada sobre las barras
A line that draws itself: a chart whose: Una línea que se dibuja sola: una gráfica cuyas líneas suben con un punto en cada punta y el valor final que aparece; un trayecto ondulado con hitos que aparecen y una bandera; o una línea de latido que cruza de lado a lado.
A line under the face (empty = none): Una línea bajo la cara (vacío = nada)
A line under the pile (empty = none): Una línea bajo el montón (vacío = nada)
A line with a soft area: Una línea con un área suave
A list on a wheel: items roll up past th: Una lista en una rueda: los elementos suben pasando por el centro de uno en uno; el actual en negrita y oscuro, el resto más pequeños y más tenues cuanto más lejos, como el selector de un móvil.
A list that builds one line at a time: a: Una lista que se forma línea a línea: un check se dibuja solo (o se marca una casilla, un número, un punto), las palabras entran deslizándose a su lado y la lista se recentra al crecer; las líneas anteriores pueden atenuarse.
A lock-screen clock above (glass look): Un reloj de pantalla de bloqueo encima (look Cristal)
A logo sting: a rounded square drops, la: Una cortinilla de logo: un cuadrado redondeado cae, aterriza aplastándose, se convierte en un círculo y dentro aparece la letra (o tu logo), y el nombre aparece debajo - o la marca entra girando.
A loose pile of cards shuffles - the top: Un montón suelto de tarjetas se baraja - la de arriba sale y pasa debajo, una y otra vez - y luego una tarjeta se adelanta, se endereza y se ilumina con un borde brillante mientras las demás se oscurecen. Pagos, membresías, elecciones, una revelación.
A map pin drops and bounces, rings pulse: Una chincheta cae en el mapa y rebota, de su punta salen anillos sin parar y encima aparece una tarjeta con el lugar; si quieres, antes un mapa cuyas calles se dibujan solas.
A map under it (streets drawn in): Un mapa debajo (con las calles dibujándose)
A month card pops in and its days fill o: Aparece la tarjeta de un mes y sus días se llenan uno tras otro con puntos de color, con un contador de racha que avanza con ellos - un hábito, un plan de publicaciones, una cuenta atrás hasta una fecha.
A news-style band: a BREAKING tag snaps: Una banda de noticias: entra de golpe una etiqueta de última hora (BREAKING), de ella sale la barra del titular, debajo pasa un rótulo con sus líneas y parpadea un punto de directo; sale por donde entró. Para un momento de última hora en broma o una noticia de verdad.
A one- or two-line title whose letters n: Un título de una o dos líneas cuyas letras nunca se quedan quietas: las recorre una onda que las aplasta y las estira, o tiemblan como un dibujo a mano; la segunda línea en cuatro colores.
